artists.biography:
Crowded House are a pop rock band formed in Melbourne, Australia in 1985 by lead-vocalist and primary songwriter, New Zealand-born Neil Finn. Other members have included his brother Tim Finn, Australians Paul Hester, Nick Seymour and Peter Jones and Americans Mark Hart and Matt Sherrod.
Crowded House has won several national and international awards. In Australia, the group has won eleven ARIA Awards from 26 nominations, including the inaugural Best New Talent award in 1987. The majority of their ARIAs were awarded for their first two albums, Crowded House and Temple of Low Men. They won eight APRA Awards from eleven nominations and were nominated for The New Zealand Silver Scroll for "Don't Stop Now" in 2007.
"Don't Dream It's Over" was named the seventh best Australian song of all time in 2001.

perplexity.description:
Time on Earth is the fifth studio album by New Zealand-Australian rock band Crowded House, originally released in 2007 on Parlophone. Marking the band's first studio album since their 1993 breakup, Time on Earth blends melodic pop and rock with introspective lyrics and lush arrangements. The album was produced by Ethan Johns and Steve Lillywhite, with Neil Finn and Nick Seymour playing central roles in its creation. Musically, it features a mix of acoustic textures, atmospheric keyboards, and Finn's signature songwriting, reflecting both personal and collective themes of loss, renewal, and resilience.

In the context of Crowded House's discography, Time on Earth stands as a significant comeback, reuniting Finn and Seymour with new drummer Matt Sherrod following the death of original drummer Paul Hester. The album's sound is both familiar and evolved, drawing on the band's classic pop sensibilities while incorporating subtle modern production touches. Commercially, Time on Earth was well received, becoming Crowded House's highest-charting studio album in the UK, where it debuted at number three. Critics praised its emotional depth and craftsmanship, cementing its place as a thoughtful and resonant chapter in the band's legacy.
